claims.text: Multicomponent high-entropy-alloy liquids near their melting temperatures exhibit complex atomic configurations.
Traditional EAM references do not adequately represent the structural variability of the ab initio liquid.
An ML potential should replace the traditional EAM reference in thermodynamic integration.
The proposed ML potential incorporates high-dimensional descriptors of local atomic environments.
High-dimensional local-environment descriptors allow the ML potential to capture a broader range of liquid atomic configurations than EAM.
The ML potential will model complex interactions and configurational variations in the liquid more accurately than EAM.
Greater configurational fidelity will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
The proposed ML reference will improve phase-space overlap in both solid and liquid HEA states near melting.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will be reduced by at least 30% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Using the ML reference will produce free energies that align more closely with direct ab initio benchmarks.
The method applies to equiatomic or near-equiatomic HEAs.
The applicable temperature range is at or just below or above the alloys' melting temperatures.
The expected improvement is limited to compositions similar to those represented in the ML training set.
Large composition or temperature deviations from the training domain may fall outside the ML potential's effective range.
The cited records provide no eligible supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations.
The precise quantitative improvement and transferability limits of the ML potential remain uncertain.
